questions.question: $\nThe$ ratio x\/y on completion of the above reaction is _________.<\/div>$\n$
questions.explanation:
**Question Explanation:
$ The$ question asks for the ratio (x/y) of the moles of Grignard reagent (x mole of MeMgBr) to the moles of the starting reactant (y mole of 4-hydroxybutanal) required for the complete conversion to the given product (1,4-pentanediol).
$ $
$ $**Concept :
$ This$ question is based on reaction of grignard reagent with active hydrogen compounds and aldehydes.
$ $
$ $**Solution:
$ The$ starting material, **4-hydroxybutanal, has two functional groups that react with the Grignard reagent (MeMgBr):$ $
    $ $
  • The **alcohol (-OH) group, which has an **acidic proton (H+). This proton reacts instantly with the Grignard reagent (a strong base) in an **acid-base reaction to form an alkane (CH4$\u$200b) and the alkoxide salt. This also consumes **1 mole of MeMgBr per mole of -OH group.
    • $ $
  • The **aldehyde (-CHO) group, which undergoes **nucleophilic addition to form an alcohol. This consumes **1 mole of MeMgBr per mole of aldehyde.
    • $ $
$ $
$ Total$ moles of MeMgBr (x) consumed per mole of reactant (y) is 1+1=2. Therefore, x=2 and y = 1
$ The$ ratio x/y is 2.
$ $
$ $
$ $**Final Answer: 2

questions.question: <div style=\"text-align:justify\">Let f(x) be a third-degree polynomial with real coefficients satisfying<br \/>$\n$|f(1)| = |f(2)| = |f(3)| = |f(5)| = |f(6)| = |f(7)| = 12. Then |f(0)| is:<\/div>$\n$
questions.explanation: <div style=\"text-align:justify\">Without loss of generality assume that f(x) has a positive leading coefficient. Polynomial f(x) has degree 3, so each of f(x) + 12 and f(x) – 12 has at most three distinct roots. Because 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 are among these combined roots, each polynomial has precisely three of these as roots. Because f has a local maximum at a point a and a local minimum at a point b where a < b, f increases on the interval (–∞, a), decreases on the interval (a, b), and increases on the interval (b, ∞). This shows that f(x) must be equal to –12 at x = 1, 5, and 6 and equal to 12 at x = 2, 3, and 7. Thus if f(x) has leading coefficient c, then f(x) – 12 = c(x – 2) (x –3) (x – 7), so f(x) = c(x – 2) (x – 3) (x – 7) + 12. Similarly f(x) = c(x – 1) (x – 5) (x – 6) – 12. Then f(0) = –42c + 12 = –30c –12 implying that c = 2 and |f(0)| = 72.<\/div>$\n$
